56: BABÁYEV. I asked you to come with me.

38: AFÓNYA. You lie, lie! LUKÉRYA. Leave me alone! Why are you worrying me? Why did you leave grandfather?

36: LUKÉRYA. Maybe she has gone. AFÓNYA. Did she just slip out of the gate?

27: TATYÁNA. He said, not sooner than an hour. LUKÉRYA. Now you might run over. I was just there—he's waiting. He leaves to-day.

25: TATYÁNA alone TATYÁNA. [ As soon as her husband goes ] Well, good-by! At last he's gone! I'm unfortunate, unfortunate! They say one ought to love one's husband; but how can I love him? He's vulgar, uneducated—and he fondles me as a bear would! Sits there—and swaggers like a peasant; and I have to pretend to love him, to humor him; how disgusting! I'd give anything on earth not to have to do that. But how can I help it! I have to submit to one I don't love! [ Silence ] I wonder where everybody is? Here I am all alone! Such loneliness! [ Sits down at the window ] Even the streets are deserted, and there's no one to look at. Where's my sister? [ Sings softly .

[ Kisses her ] To-day I'll go and collect some money, and to-morrow I'll buy you a new outfit.
